passage:
"Mummy, no, no!" Simran clutched Rekha's kurta with both hands at the school gate.
"I know it is hard, Simran. I will be back after your lunch, when the bell rings. I will wait right here at this gate."
"Stay!"
"Not today. A big hug, then one kiss on the count of three?"
Simran squeezed her tight, sobbing.
Rekha loosened the small fingers gently and walked her to the teacher. "See you after lunch, jaan." She waved once from the gate and did not sneak away.
Simran wailed but watched her go, then let the teacher hold her hand.

qa.q: When did Rekha say she would come back?
qa.a: She said she would be back after Simran's lunch, when the bell rings.

qa.q: How does Simran feel at the gate?
qa.a: She feels deep sadness at the separation: she clutches the kurta with both hands, sobs and begs her mother to stay.

qa.q: What did Rekha do that made parting easier?
qa.a: She said a short kind goodbye, told Simran exactly when she would return, hugged her, and did not sneak away.

qa.q: Why might it have been worse if Rekha lingered or slipped away?
qa.a: Lingering would drag out the pain, and sneaking off might make Simran fear Mummy could vanish, so she would cling harder next time.

grounding: A child holds her mother's kurta and cries at the school gate; the parent says a short kind goodbye, names when she will return and does not sneak away.

passage:
Note from Kishore, class teacher, Monday and Tuesday.
Monday: At the gate Shankar held on to his mother's dress and cried. His mother kissed him, walked away, then came back three times to comfort him. Each time she returned, he cried harder. He cried most of the morning.
I spoke to her at pick-up about a short goodbye.
Tuesday: She hugged him once and said, "I will come when the lunch bell rings." Then she waved and left, without turning back. Shankar cried at the gate, but stopped by the time we reached the classroom. At lunch bell he ran to the gate and she was there.

qa.q: How many times did Shankar's mother come back on Monday?
What does Shankar crying harder each time his mother returned suggest?
qa.a: It suggests the goodbye felt scarier and more confusing each time; his fear of her leaving grew instead of settling.

qa.q: What did Shankar's mother change on Tuesday, and why did it help?
qa.a: She gave one hug, told him when she would return and left without turning back, so the goodbye was short and clear.

qa.q: How might Shankar's mother have felt walking away on Tuesday?
qa.a: She may have felt torn and sad leaving him crying, but her waiting at the lunch bell showed him she kept her word.

grounding: A child clings to his mother's dress at the school gate; lingering makes it harder, while a short kind goodbye that says when she will return helps.

passage:
At the village school gate, Zubin gripped Ammi's dupatta in both fists and wailed.
Zeenat bent down. She could see the teacher waving the children in with the bell. It would be easy to slip away while Zubin watched the goats by the wall. She had done that once at her sister's house, and he had screamed for an hour.
So she stayed and looked into his eyes. "Zubin, I am going home now. I will come back when the school bell rings after lunch. Right here."
She hugged him once and walked away without looking back. At the wall, she heard his crying grow smaller.

qa.q: What was Zubin holding at the school gate?
qa.a: He gripped Ammi's dupatta in both fists.

qa.q: What was Zeenat worried about when she thought of slipping away?
qa.a: She worried he would feel tricked and frightened, remembering that he screamed for an hour when she sneaked away at her sister's house.

qa.q: Which choice did Zeenat make, and why was it wise?
qa.a: She said a short kind goodbye and told him when she would come back, instead of sneaking off, so he could trust her.

qa.q: How might the goodbye feel to Zubin?
qa.a: Zubin still feels sad and cries, but because Ammi told him she was going and when she would return, his crying grows smaller.

grounding: A young child clings to his mother at the school gate; she chooses a short, kind goodbye with a clear return time instead of sneaking away.
